Team — proposed language and negotiation points below. I kept it tight to reduce commercial pushback. Draft ready to send to PioneerWorks counsel if Sergio signs off.

Suggested legal response (summary):
1) Injunctive carveout (limited): "Notwithstanding the dispute resolution provisions, either party may seek provisional or injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction solely to preserve rights or protect confidential information, subject to immediate notice to the other party and without prejudice to the exclusive forum provision for the merits of any claim."

2) Forum allocation (compromise): "The parties agree that, except for provisional relief as set forth above, the exclusive forum for disputes on the merits shall be the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware. Notwithstanding the foregoing, if both parties mutually agree in writing, the parties may litigate in the United States District Court for the Northern District of California."

3) Preservation window / limited discovery: Insert a clause establishing a 7-calendar-day preservation window after notice where the parties may take narrowly tailored preservation steps (metadata snapshot, limited forensic collection) without waiving forum rights. Kate / Marcus — thanks for the redline and for being flexible on this. We want to keep the merits forum predictable (Delaware) but are willing to accept a narrow, reciprocal provisional relief carveout limited to preservation and confidentiality measures. Below is the operationally-focused compromise we can sign off on: 

1) Carveout: Either party may seek provisional relief (injunctive or preservation orders) in any competent court solely to preserve evidence or confidential information; such relief shall be narrowly tailored and temporary, and the parties agree that the merits of any dispute shall remain subject to the exclusive forum provision unless otherwise mutually agreed in writing.

2) Forum on merits: Delaware Court of Chancery as default; NDCA available only by mutual written election.

3) Preservation window: 7-calendar-day preservation period after written notice for narrow evidence collection; Redwood will provide a mechanism for an export of logs/metadata for Dedicated and Private customers within that window where reasonably requested and subject to standard security/ops controls.
